definitions.gloss: to push up, to shove upward
definitions.explanation: To physically push something upward using force.

definitions.gloss: to boost, to drive up, to elevate
definitions.explanation: To raise or increase something, such as numbers, rankings, or status. Commonly used in economics and business contexts.

examples.japanese: {重|おも}い{荷物|にもつ}を{棚|たな}に{押|お}し{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: I pushed the heavy luggage up onto the shelf.

examples.japanese: {波|なみ}がボートを{押|お}し{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: The waves pushed the boat upward.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}で{協力|きょうりょく}して{岩|いわ}を{押|お}し{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: The two of us worked together to push the rock up.

examples.japanese: {円安|えんやす}が{輸出|ゆしゅつ}を{押|お}し{上|あ}げた。
{新商品|しんしょうひん}の{売|う}れ{行|ゆ}きが{業績|ぎょうせき}を{押|お}し{上|あ}げている。
examples.english: Sales of the new product are boosting the company's performance.

examples.japanese: {原油|げんゆ}{価格|かかく}の{上昇|じょうしょう}が{物価|ぶっか}を{押|お}し{上|あ}げる{要因|よういん}になっている。
examples.english: Rising crude oil prices are a factor driving up consumer prices.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound verb combining {押|お}す (to push) and {上|あ}げる (to raise). The literal sense (sense 1) describes physical upward force. The figurative sense (sense 2) is very common in news and business contexts, where it describes factors that increase numbers or improve outcomes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {業績|ぎょうせき}を{押|お}し{上|あ}げる: to boost performance
- {物価|ぶっか}を{押|お}し{上|あ}げる: to drive up prices
- {順位|じゅんい}を{押|お}し{上|あ}げる: to push up rankings

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {引|ひ}き{上|あ}げる: to raise, to pull up (more deliberate, policy-driven)
- {持|も}ち{上|あ}げる: to lift up (with hands, from below)
